name: Question 17
problem:
Evaluate the double integral
${∬}_{D}\frac{1}{yx\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dA,$
where $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the lines
$x=e,$ $y=e$ and the curve $y={e}^{x}.$
worked_solution:
Let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/aa635ca5ef3198fea56d684b034de476a72e4ace2a4c51b37c6c59977036eb76.png)

Notice that $D$ is a type I region.

- The line $y=e$ intercepts the curve $y={e}^{x}$ at $x=1.$
So, the $x$-limits are 
$1\le x\le e.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/b78021a06c9fea100b75c66a619c425345cda3666d84da018895be15a53af06d.png)

As a result, the integral is defined over the following type I region: 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,e\le y\le {e}^{x}}
$$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}\frac{1}{yx\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dA={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{x}}\frac{1}{yx\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dy\,dx
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{x}}\frac{1}{yx\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}[{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{x}}\frac{1}{y\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)]}_{e}^{{e}^{x}}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{x})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡e))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}dx & ={[\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{2}]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡e}{2}-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's make a sketch of our region.

Notice that D is a type I region.

  • The line y=e intercepts the curve y=ex at x=1. So, the x-limits are 1≤x≤e.

  • To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

As a result, the integral is defined over the following type I region:

D={(x,y):1≤x≤e,e≤y≤ex}

So, we can express the integral as follows:

∬D1yxln⁡ydA=∫1e∫eex1yxln⁡ydydx

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to y, treating x as a constant:

∫1e∫eex1yxln⁡ydydx=∫1e1x[∫eex1yln⁡ydy]dx=∫1e1x[ln⁡(ln⁡y)]eexdx=∫1e1x(ln⁡(ln⁡ex)−ln⁡(ln⁡e))dx=∫1eln⁡xxdx

Then, we integrate with respect to x:

∫1eln⁡xxdx=[ln2⁡x2]1e=ln2⁡e2−ln2⁡12=12
